sprint.name: Sprint 3: clear scanner outcomes and reliable sync
sprint.goal: Give scanner operators exact Entry rejection reasons and current queue/sync feedback, and retain the combined denial and mixed-sync journeys in the maintained browser suite.

outcome.headline: Scanner operators get exact Entry refusal reasons and accurate queue and storage-wait feedback. Ready for the owner close decision; no tag or deployment.
outcome.summary:
All eleven functional members are Done. The owner added four correction members after round 3: TKT-574 fixed the storage-wait acceptance defect, TKT-577 fixed the unknown-cost label, TKT-578 patched Go to 1.27.4 for GO-2026-6859, and TKT-581 repaired the historical browser builds after the pnpm 11.12.0 deprecation.

Round 4, the last round under the four-round cap, reviewed the frozen candidate b836c902 with gpt-6-luna at high effort in all four areas. Implementation approved with zero findings. Verification, retrospective and documentation raised Medium findings only; none was Critical or High. The DOC-1 guide correction is commit 60d570d7, the final candidate, with a fresh passing gate. It changes only docs/testing.md.

The gate passed at the final candidate. Browser, security, hermetic and Go-identity executions ran at merged main 5bbb14d3 or TKT-578 head 40e75699 and keep those identities; the candidate differs from 5bbb14d3 only in two guides. Native visibility ran at b836c902. Maintained B2 stays synthetic; sleep, suspension and bfcache are not claimed.

Open limits: the historical French checkout timeout (TKT-573), the unexplained App.exit test failure (TKT-583), the smoke.sh SIGPIPE race (TKT-584), the tracked S-2 evidence rewrite (TKT-582) and Docker port-forward failures on one smoke slot. All are Low and non-blocking. Coverage, complexity, active time, CI wait and spend stay unknown where records do not establish them. The historical clean-host bootstrap is unverified.

This report claims no owner close approval, tag or deployment. The owner close decision must name the candidate, the report commit, path and HTML digest, and the brief and scope digests.

scope.summary:
The original scope was TKT-512, TKT-565, TKT-566 and closure task TKT-567. The owner approved eight additions: TKT-568, TKT-569, TKT-570 and TKT-571 before round 3, then TKT-574 and TKT-577 after the round 3 documentation audit, then TKT-578 and TKT-581 during the correction work. All twelve remain members. The eleven functional members are Done. TKT-567 remains Building until the owner close decision. No member was removed.

TKT-572, TKT-573, TKT-575, TKT-576, TKT-582, TKT-583 and TKT-584 are Backlog follow-ups outside S-3. The full baseline-to-candidate measurement includes external dependency, documentation and workflow changes. It is not a measurement of sprint-authored work alone.

It verified sprint identity, the final candidate, scope, area records, the readiness, approval and publication states, every board pointer and the HTML. retrospective.summary:
Cutoff: 2026-11-20T06:03:16+00:00, when TKT-578 became Done. Closure-task work after that instant is excluded. The board capture at 06:31:48Z shows four originally committed members, eight approved additions, twelve members, eleven Done and one open closure task. No member was removed and no membership history gap was reported. The packet's earlier 05:37:22Z snapshot predates TKT-578 Done and is not used for counts.

For the seven members reviewed in round 3, primary synthesis counts 84 plan finding groups over 18 ticket-rounds: 83 fixed and one historical owner-accepted package-age risk. It counts eight code finding groups over nine ticket-rounds: seven fixed and one originally deferred, with zero rejected. The deferred TKT-512 A1 group was later remediated through separate dependency repairs. That repair does not rewrite its original disposition. The round 3 decision audit confirms the 84 plan-group and 18 plan-round totals. Its correction preserves the original code-review deferral separately from later remediation. Earlier review results remain unchanged. Reused IDs are not global defect identities. A TKT-512 fixture fix introduced a separate later defect, and the TKT-568 disclosure finding remains separate from the risk it describes.

Historical independence was uneven. Same-model reviews under owner D18 include TKT-512 code round 2; both TKT-565 stages; TKT-568 plan rounds 7-8 and code round 2; and TKT-571 plan rounds 1-3 when primary COS text is counted. Other records name different models, but execution metadata is missing for the TKT-568 plan round 6 and TKT-569 plan round 1, and null for the TKT-570 code round 1. Recorded IDs do not prove execution identity. The primary-authored COS text in TKT-571 counts as authorship. Recorded distinct full IDs must not be collapsed into aliases. These exceptions do not authorize same-model final review.

Owner steering on October 22 did not promptly replace older routing clauses. The owner clarified the final-review choice before this cutoff. The newly discovered external workflow authorship later invalidated the first final-review attempt. The report keeps that failure visible and does not convert its useful findings into independent approval.

The retained operation ledger has 171 entries and covers only the November TKT-566, TKT-570 and TKT-571 campaigns. It omits the October members and includes overlapping parent and child operations. Successful operations, intentional mutation failures, usage errors and board-availability failures are different outcomes. They are not a single gate-failure count.

Implementation time: n/a. Review time: n/a. Exclusive verification time: n/a. CI wait: n/a. Unexplained idle: n/a. The records cannot separate these costs. Board status durations are elapsed attribution, including unattended waits, not productive work. Financial spend is separately n/a because retained billing is incomplete. Individual executed command durations are listed as such in measurements. Coverage and complexity remain unmeasured for the stated tool limits.

The design signal is concentrated sync and queue-observation state in App.tsx, with extensive rendering-tier interleaving tests. A plain-module extraction is a future design candidate; this closure task makes no architectural change. The process proposals below also remain pending human selection. No proposal has been adopted automatically.

The eight TKT-568 plan rounds retain their owner-steering references D14, D19, D25 and D27 for rounds 5-8. Round 5 followed a premature contract call, round 6 a new Go basis, round 7 the R6-I1 correction, and round 8 Undici scope. Round 7 used the primary interpretation of the next-pass wording from the owner; that wording did not name a new numeric limit. These historical extensions do not reset the current final-review cap. The package-age exception is historical owner acceptance, not a completed fix; its exposure ended when the package matured.

Scope additions after review began are a repeated pattern. The owner approved TKT-574 and TKT-577 after the round 3 documentation audit, then TKT-578 and TKT-581 during that correction work. Each addition needed its own pipeline, fresh proof and a new frozen packet, while only one sprint-review round remained under the cap. Nothing recorded the remaining review capacity at approval time. Candidate P10 proposes that check.

Correction members, by the same counting: TKT-574, TKT-577 and TKT-578 passed plan and code review in one round each. TKT-581 needed three plan rounds for a 24-line test change because its execution context and evidence binding were under-specified, and its code audit found two unenforced evidence drivers. TKT-577's one-line fix carried a large proof plan; its closeout judged that cost proportionate for an owner-signed report.
